absent: Numeric ceilings for virtual CPUs per controller generation.
Exact bit positions and widths of hardware feature registers used for list depth derivation.
Full field list of the firmware topology descriptor beyond observed resources and flags.
Complete device operation contracts for versioned controllers and the translation service.
Encoding of hypervisor mapping permission kinds for code data and device memory.
Bounds allocation policy and exhaustion handling of the hypervisor private address allocator.
Contract guarantees and failure modes of the protected initialization hypercall.
Lifetime and invalidation rules for hypervisor mappings after teardown paths.
Definitions of CPU interface trap bits and their selective performance effects.
Architectural identifiers for implemented private interrupts and their enablement protocol.
Release pairing and ordering for the paging mutex on paths whose unlock helper is outside listed stubs.
Entropy and lifetime guarantees for hypervisor pointer authentication keys.

findings.text: Probes for GICv2 GICv3 and GICv5 form the guest capability establishment interface, each accepting firmware topology and publishing generation selection and emulation capability in shared state with a status result.
Generation based device registration installs the appropriate virtual controller operations, with GICv3 implicitly chaining translation service installation as part of its contract.

Contract for device region mapping promises paired kernel and hypervisor visibility on success and no residual mapping on failure, with protected mode always refused and hypervisor privileged execution collapsing the pair to a single shared mapping.
Hypervisor memory management offers table creation, guarded stack allocation, table teardown and paging structure destruction as the externally reachable memory lifecycle interface.
Operating mode query plus CPU interface trap activation together expose mode awareness and on demand trapping enablement driven by hardware capability reporting.
Protected execution forbids GICv2 emulation establishment and GICv5 guest enablement, while GICv3 probing continues with compatibility optionally reduced.
Active list register depth is derived afresh during each successful probe from the associated hardware feature register, subject to architectural capping that discards excess high bits.

Shared VGIC state consistently records controller generation, list depth, emulation permission, relevant base addresses and virtual CPU ceiling after probe, with the newest generation initially clearing legacy translation flags.

Implemented private interrupt set for the newest generation always includes architectural timer sources and the software source, with the performance monitor source present exactly when the platform reports monitor support.

Hypervisor virtual address establishment validates table geometry against requested address width, rejects identity map overlap with the hypervisor range, and records the address width plus IO allocation base for later private mappings.

Hypervisor image mapping preserves distinct access rights across executable, writable and read only regions, with stack and per CPU areas established before symbolic propagation and optional protection.

Hypervisor visible architecture feature values are sanitized for speculation vulnerability reporting before propagation, and fine grained trap mask collections are mirrored into hypervisor symbols followed by cache maintenance for early boot visibility.

Protected bring up assigns fresh random pointer authentication keys per physical CPU in hypervisor context and converts host scalable vector state pointers into hypervisor addressable form during finalization.
Destruction of the hypervisor top level paging structures is serialized by a dedicated global mutex that is held across lookup, destruction and nullification.
Reservation of private virtual range for hypervisor stacks is serialized by the same global paging mutex, held only across the reservation step and released before backing store mapping.

Firmware descriptor observed by probes carries control interface and CPU interface resource descriptions with start addresses, a CPU base address where relevant, and boolean capability indicators for newer translation features.

Shared controller state aggregates generation selector, list depth, emulation and translation capability flags, kernel and hypervisor base pointers for control and CPU interfaces, plus virtual CPU ceiling and compatibility branch state.

Hypervisor paging descriptor carries address width, computed start level, memory operation hooks, optional owner and forcing callback, plus a root reference that is cleared after destruction, while the walker pairs a freeing callback with leaf and postorder traversal modes.

Probe lifecycle moves from mode and resource validation through conditional mapping and trap configuration into device registration and global activation, with any failure transitioning to cleanup that releases acquired mappings and registrations.

Hypervisor mode bring up advances from paging foundation through image, stack and per CPU mapping into symbol propagation and optional protected sealing, where any failure diverts to a unified teardown that frees stacks, per CPU areas, vector state and paging.
Generation probes and generation dispatch registration constitute the creation time entry surface through which firmware topology results in guest visible interrupt controller types.
Initial paging creation, guarded stack allocation and paired IO mapping constitute the memory bring up entry surface used before hypervisor execution is fully enabled.
Unaligned or absent CPU interface resources do not abort probing but force trap based emulation with reduced performance or silent disabling of backward compatibility, depending on generation.
Failure after partial acquisition must release mappings and device registrations, otherwise stale mappings or half registered generations would persist into later guest creation.
Overlap between the identity map page and the hypervisor virtual range aborts address space creation, and dispersal of initialization code across page boundaries is treated as fatal.

Protected sealing depends on preallocated protected memory, successful relay setup, host vector state allocation and firmware workaround acknowledgement, with any unsatisfied prerequisite aborting hypervisor initialization.

Hypervisor stack integrity depends on size aligned reservation of a doubled extent where only the upper half is backed, allowing overflow detection via address bit testing. Misaligned reservation would break that detection.
Distinct device type selectors identify GICv2 GICv3 GICv5 and the translation service for registration and lookup.
Each controller generation defines its own ceiling on virtual CPUs, with combined operation constrained by the most restrictive applicable ceiling.
Separate mapping permission kinds distinguish executable hypervisor code, writable data, read only data and device memory for private hypervisor mappings.
Paging teardown traversal combines leaf visitation with postorder table visitation to ensure both mappings and intermediate tables are freed.
